title: Bind P104 outgoing ports to recipient histories and input admission
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR3423 left the actual histories behind its 675 outgoing ADD ports open. This source-bound audit closes those histories in the unchanged PR2586 word and identifies the additional entrance conditions. All port-cut states require 2,907 events/263 initial banks; preserving the terminal histories of all introduced dependencies stabilizes at **4,027 events/265 inputs** (including private cleanup).

Under the explicitly inherited native covariance and Newton-module premises, every retained atomic state admits the sharp independent dyadic product entrance: 104 Y inputs in `4B9`, 38 N inputs in `2B9`, and 123 others in `B9`. At event 312, `N100(x)=2*x_0` satisfies the earlier 63-bank admission but its exact integer half leaves `B9`. The complete terminal Y map has rank **9**, certified by a factorization of all 52×104 entries and a minor of determinant `-1/128`. The inherited `2032H` payload bound is specialized, not claimed as new.

This is a conditional interface certificate, not a paid supplier or κ improvement. It explicitly lists **696 omitted outgoing ADDs to 93 omitted banks**; the projection does not preserve those side effects. Native semantics, input preparation, physical storage/routing/temporaries and recursive costs remain obligations. The selected frontier and unchanged-profile `599/584` stop are unchanged.

## Task and overlap

- Base main: `6f100d4bb5083f8c35d96fd95a539811c62f245c`.
- Task `p104-side-correction`, scope **changed** to the [released PR3423 handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2750#discussioncomment-19009429); exact predecessor `15d28c4de37dc47ea07cd7173c8b318fca7a4d75`.
- [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2750#discussioncomment-19009569). Entry checks covered 353 open PRs and 2,277 Discussion records with complete pagination; publication refresh found no competing recipient-closure artifact. Unpublished work and exhaustive historical diffs are excluded.
- Complements #3423 (open ports), #3406 (whole-word product domain), #3416 (native covariance), and #3426 (correlated final-cut admission). Runtime uses only the two unchanged source files already on main, not unmerged predecessor executables.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only. At `886222c1d3e2c2d878b263dc8d165ef03d5bac7f`:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-external-port-closure
python3.12 -I -O -B research/p104-external-port-closure/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p104-external-port-closure --check-source-history
```

All PASS. The 11-file source-bound archive passed export/check and isolated optimized replay with Git unavailable. Separate SSA and reverse-liveness implementations agree on exact closure sets. Checks include 142 weakened-admission controls, eight rejection groups, two rank regressions, exact rank witnesses, three full-word/projection scalar fixtures, and exact Newton negative/positive controls. A review-found rank-routine error was corrected before publication and recorded in TASK.json. Finite checks support the conditional proof in PROOF.md; no heavy native replay, Lean check, or selected-frontier replay was run.

Detailed provenance is in README.md and SOURCES.json.

## Open next questions

The [package's next questions](research/p104-external-port-closure/README.md#open-next-questions) start with supplying and paying for the 265-bank admission, or accounting for the 696 omitted side effects. Neither justifies another unchanged-profile supplier round; any changed profile first needs a compatible full cost screen.
